figures.finding: Salaries tax is the lower of progressive rates on net chargeable income (2%, 6%, 10%, 14% on successive HK$50,000 bands, 17% on the remainder) and the standard rate on net income before allowances (15% on the first HK$5 million, 16% above).

value.rule: min(progressive on net chargeable income, standard on net income before allowances)

figures.applies: Years of assessment 2024/25 onwards until superseded (so 2026/27); no regional layer.

sources.said: Tax payable is calculated at progressive rates on your net chargeable income or at standard rate on your net income (before deduction of the allowances), whichever is lower.
Two-tiered Standard Rates On the first $5,000,000 of net income - 15% Remainder - 16%

figures.finding: The year of assessment runs from 1 April to 31 March; the individual return (BIR60) is due within one month of issue (three months with a sole-proprietor business); provisional salaries tax for the coming year is charged with the assessment and paid 75% around January and 25% around April.

figures.finding: No tax is withheld from pay: salaries tax is assessed on the employee and collected with provisional salaries tax based on the prior year's income; Hong Kong imposes no withholding tax.
figures.applies: Residents' salaries and freelance fees (a self-employed person pays profits tax by assessment).

sources.said: Notably, Hong Kong does not impose sales tax, VAT, withholding tax, capital gains tax, estate tax, or dividend tax.

figures.finding: Employee and employer each pay 5% of relevant income into MPF, with no employee contribution below HK$7,100 a month and a cap at HK$30,000 (HK$1,500 each); a self-employed person pays 5% between HK$85,200 and HK$360,000 a year (max HK$18,000).

sources.said: Employees and employers are both required to make mandatory contributions of 5% of the employee’s relevant income into the employee’s MPF account, subject to the minimum and maximum relevant income levels.
For monthly paid employees, the current minimum and maximum relevant income levels are $7,100 and $30,000 respectively.

Less than $7,100/month (or $85,200/year) Not required $7,100 to $30,000/month (or $85,200 to $360,000/year) Relevant income x 5% More than $30,000/month (or $360,000/year) $1,500/month (or $18,000/year)

figures.finding: A self-employed screen worker pays profits tax on an unincorporated business at 7.5% on the first HK$2 million of assessable profits and 15% above.

sources.said: Two-tiered rates Year of Assessment Tax Rates 2018/19 onwards 7.5% on assessable profits up to $2,000,000; and 15% on any part of assessable profits over $2,000,000

figures.finding: A non-resident entertainer is charged profits tax (15%, or 7.5% on the first HK$2 million) on the gross sum less one-third deemed expenses, assessed in the Hong Kong payer's name; the payer retains 10% of the gross (11% through a corporate agent) to settle it. Performance includes films and television.
